newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Direction sought from Aramco.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Direction sought from Aramco.

text.p: Gasoline was actively sold amid news of Saudi Aramco's decision not to award its gasoline tender but some traders were still bullish on April with good Asian demand, traders said on Friday.
Aramco decided not to buy up to 1.5 million barrels of gasoline for April delivery due to the high offer prices, traders said.
"We heard Aramco compared the prices at which it has sold cargoes and the offers it received, and saw such a big difference it decided not to buy," said one trader.
He said Aramco has sold 95-octane unleaded cargoes at $2.00-$3.00 per barrel over Singapore naphtha quotes on a free-on-board basis.

Offers into this tender for 95-octane 0.4 grammes per litre tender, however, were at a premium of $5.00-$6.00 per barrel over the same Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis to Ras Tanura in the MidEast gulf.
The tender closed on March 4 and was valid until March 12.
Another trader said Aramco might defer its requirements to May.

Buyers said they were still in the market to buy ahead of the strong U.S. driving season and amid good regional demand as Chinese refineries head into turnarounds and dwindling supplies of low-octane Russian supplies prompt Vietnamese demand.
Naphtha April swaps rose to $23.50/$23.60 from $23.25/23.40, on Friday, firming amid good North Asian demand.

Gasoline edged down slightly with the European major offering cargoes this week, emerging again on Friday.

But some players were bullish and four buyers bought 50,000 barrels each - a European major bought 97-octane at $28.80 per barrel for April 9-13 lifting, two shosha paid $28.75 and $28.55 for 95-octane lifting April 4-8 and March 31-April 5 respectively, while a Dutch trader paid $28.00 for 92-octane for April 9-13.
